messages:
Alex Kim: Quick follow-up to the fairness scheduler RFC — hit a few weird edge cases in staging when tenants run bursty short requests interleaved with long-lived streaming sessions. Need to decide the contract for session-affinity vs per-request accounting. Link to RFC: https://redwood/rfcs/fair-scheduler

Mira Patel: We observed streams keeping KV/ctx alive and bypassing per-request counters. Looks like sessions re-use a cached KV handle and never surface into the global rate counter.

Sam Ortega: For an interface boundary, I'd prefer the scheduler exposes a small LeaseRequest/LeaseResponse proto instead of peeking into runtime internals. Example:
```
message LeaseRequest {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  string session_id = 2; // optional
  int32 tokens = 3;
  uint32 priority = 4;
}
message LeaseResponse {
  bool allowed = 1;
  int32 granted = 2; // tokens
  string reason = 3;
}
```
Runtime calls scheduler synchronously, gets granted tokens and attaches them to the request. Keeps runtime stateless.

Kyle Zhang: Stateless is nice for the runtime but we need global fairness across replicas. Suggest a two-tier design: local fast-path counters with conservative local burst allowance + a regional LeaseCoordinator for long-term fairness. Fast path handles ~95% of requests, coordinator arbitrates heavy hitters. Fallback budget should be tiny (e.g., <= 200 tokens) and decision latency for fallback < 2ms.

Alex Kim: Agree on two-tier. Tradeoffs:
- Local counters: low latency, but divergence under failover.
- Central coord: consistent fairness, but adds tail latency and operational complexity.

Proposed compromise: keep local elastic buckets that sync heartbeats to coordinator every 2s. Coordinator only intervenes when a tenant's local spend crosses a threshold (burst_ratio > 3x expected). That limits coordinator load.

Mira Patel: Also: we need to attribute KV cache hits to the originating session. Suggest attaching `session_id` and `lease_token` to cached entries so replays decrement the same bucket. Otherwise streams cheat the quota.

Jordan Lee: On abuse detection — we should add a lightweight score per tenant that combines sudden QPS delta + error rate + prompt entropy heuristics. Score > X triggers soft-throttle and elevated logging. Hard blocks only for repeated confirmed abuse. Soft-throttle policy:
- 5s soft window, degrade to 50% throughput
- escalate to coordinator if persists > 30s

Sam Ortega: Migration plan proposal:
1) Add telemetry: per-tenant spend, session attribution, cache-hit attribution, burst_ratio, fairness_gini.
2) Implement local fast-path + coordinator in staging behind a feature flag.
3) Opt-in 10% tenant beta with shadow mode enforcement (simulated denies logged, not enforced).
4) Gradual enforcement and rollback safety toggles.

Alex Kim: Metrics to track during rollout: p50/p95 latency, denied_rate, coordinator_qps, token_replenish_rate, fairness_gini, incidents per hour, and number of sessions with stale attribution. Also add a dashboard for 'abuse score' spikes + sample prompts for triage.

Kyle Zhang: One more practical thing — billing and SLAs. If we change the billing unit from per-request to token-anchored session accounting, we must keep a clear migration mapping. Proposal: for 3 months dual-reporting (old vs new) and line-item reconciliation for customers on Dedicated.

Mira Patel: Implementation nit: keep the LeaseRequest small and language-agnostic. Provide SDK helpers that automatically attach session_id + lease_token. That keeps most callers simple.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: scheduler v0.2 rolled out to staging at 2026-03-15T09:12Z (canary 3 nodes)

Alex Kim: OK — next action items: Kyle to draft coordinator HA model, Mira to prototype session attribution in runtime, Sam to wire the proto and SDK hooks. I'll draft the rollout checklist and dashboards. @everyone :thumbsup:
thread_text: Quick follow-up to the fairness scheduler RFC — edge cases: bursts vs long sessions, interface boundary, coordinator vs local counters, session attribution, abuse scoring, migration plan, metrics and rollout steps
